packLunchbox.name: Pack the Lunchbox
packLunchbox.description: Split the items into a lunchbox and a rucksack: fit as many as you can into the lunchbox without going over its capacity, and put everything else in the rucksack.

solveInSixteenLines.name: Solve in 16 lines of code
solveInSixteenLines.description: Can you solve this exercise with only 16 lines of code?

everythingFits.name: Everything fits
everythingFits.description: A roomy lunchbox where every item fits, so the rucksack stays empty.

packTheMost.name: Fit the most
packTheMost.description: Space is tight, so the small items go in the lunchbox and the big ones are left for the rucksack.

justTheSnack.name: Just the snack
justTheSnack.description: Only the very smallest item fits; the rest go in the rucksack.

nothingFits.name: Nothing fits
nothingFits.description: Even the smallest item is too big, so everything ends up in the rucksack.

emptyLunchbox.name: Empty lunchbox
emptyLunchbox.description: There are no items at all, so both the lunchbox and the rucksack come back empty.

bonus1.name: 16 lines of code
bonus1.description: Solve the exercise with only 16 lines of code.

readEachItem.question: How do I get each item's name and size?
readEachItem.answer: Each item is a pair. The first part is the name and the second is the size, so you can read them out of the item one at a time.

fitTheMost.question: How do I fit in as many items as possible?
fitTheMost.answer: Think about which items to add first. Smaller items leave more room for others, so it pays to deal with them before the big ones.

goSmallestFirst.question: The items are listed largest first — how do I go through them smallest first?
goSmallestFirst.answer: There's an array method that gives you back a reversed copy of an array. Reverse the items first, then work through them in that new order.

knowWhenFull.question: How do I decide where each item goes?
knowWhenFull.answer: Keep a running total of the sizes you've added. Before adding an item, check whether the total plus its size would still fit within the capacity. If it does, it goes in the lunchbox, otherwise it goes in the rucksack.

toReversed.description: Returns a copy of the array with the elements in reverse order, without changing the original.

push.description: Adds an element onto the end of an array, changing the array in place.
